reports.subject: FUEL SURETY REVIEW CLOSED, DETACHMENT SANDPIPER ISSUES FROM TANK
reports.reported_status: Closed. BF-14 floating suction assembly restored, verified riding on float, and in aircraft issue since 1 October on closure of MAB-FMX-OI-26-074; product issued to Detachment SANDPIPER drawn in the configuration reference (c) requires, and no fuel surety item stands against the tank or the detachment.
reports.text:
E02-SS-R06
REPORT ID:  E02-SS-R06
SERIAL:     MAB-FMF-0177
PRECEDENCE: PRIORITY
DTG:        040326K OCT 26
FROM:       Fuels Management Flight, Fuel Surety Assessment Cell
TO:         Installation Watch Officer, ICC, MARISOL AB
INFO:       Senior Duty Commander (info only); Detachment SANDPIPER
            Maintenance Control; Fuels Quality Assurance; Fuels Distribution
SUBJ:       FUEL SURETY REVIEW CLOSED, DETACHMENT SANDPIPER ISSUES FROM TANK
            BF-14 DURING AND FOLLOWING A BULK RECEIPT
REF:        (a) MABI 23-201
            (b) MABI 23-110
            (c) MABI 21-402
            (d) Work Order MAB-FMX-WO-26-0561
            (e) Float Verification Record MAB-FMX-FV-26-0033
            (f) ALTORD BRIDGEWATER 26-07A, 040253K OCT 26

1. SITUATION. The Fuel Surety Assessment Cell has completed a consolidated post-restoration review of Operating Tank BF-14 covering 2000K 3 October through 0300K 4 October, the tank's first bulk receipt since its return to aircraft issue on 1 October. The review establishes that BF-14's floating suction assembly has been riding on float since the tank was restored at tank entry and returned to aircraft issue on 1 October, on closure of open item MAB-FMX-OI-26-074; that the tank took a 44,000-gallon receipt at approximately 700 gallons per minute between 0018K and 0121K; and that all three Detachment SANDPIPER aircraft were serviced from BF-14 between 0056K and 0203K, every issue drawn through the floating suction in the configuration reference (c) requires. The detachment's departure has been moved by reference (f) to 0605K, 6 October. No item is open against the tank or against the product issued, and this review is closed.
2. TANK CONFIGURATION. BF-14's floating suction assembly is riding on float. Its swing-joint cable assembly parted on 12 September, and the assembly hung at a fixed position approximately eight inches above the tank floor until the tank was restored. BF-14 was removed from aircraft issue on 12 September and held to ground fuels only; Deviation MAB-FD-26-041, raised the same day to return the tank to aircraft issue in that configuration, was returned without approval by the Fuels Management Flight Commander on 15 September, and the tank remained out of aircraft issue until the condition had been corrected and verified. Reference (c) requires aviation fuel presented for aircraft issue to be drawn through a floating suction assembly riding on float; the only route to compliance was physical work at an emptied and entered tank, and that work has been done. The contract tank entry booked for 22 October was brought forward by the Regional Fuels Engineering Activity at the Fuel Farm Systems Section's request: BF-14 was emptied and gassed free on 27-28 September and entered on 29 September under reference (d); the cable assembly was replaced from fuel farm shop stock, the float was rigged, and the assembly was verified riding on float at three product levels under reference (e), dual-signature verified with Fuels Quality Assurance; the tank was closed and refilled on 30 September and returned to aircraft issue at 1400K, 1 October, when open item MAB-FMX-OI-26-074 was closed in the maintenance record under entry MAB-FMX-MR-26-0702 and struck from the fuels maintenance board. The configuration record is current. At the Fuel Farm Systems Section's mid-shift standing check completed 0035K this date, the position indicator at the tank shell read the assembly at the product surface, and between 0035K and 0110K the pointer travelled with the level without binding or slack. No deviation, waiver, or open item stands against BF-14.
3. RECEIPT. Transfer Order MAB-TO-26-1188 moved 44,000 gallons from Bulk Storage Tank BS-1 to BF-14, commencing 0018K and completing 0121K. Meter advance and tank gauge increase agree to within 60 gallons. A receipt sample was drawn at completion, was clear and bright on appearance, and returned a conforming screening result at 0244K. That sample characterizes the product delivered by the transfer.
4. ISSUES. BF-14 issued to SANDPIPER ONE (8,100 gallons, 0056K), SANDPIPER TWO (9,250 gallons, 0129K), and SANDPIPER THREE (7,940 gallons, 0203K) by way of refuelers filled at the truck fill stand. Visual appearance, aqua-detector, and conductivity checks were completed at each issue and recorded within limits. All three issues reconcile against their tickets. Each issue was drawn through BF-14's floating suction riding on float, near the product surface.
5. TANK BOTTOM CONDITION. Material resident on a tank floor, together with water and fines carried in with a receipt, requires approximately three hours to fall out of suspension at current product temperatures, which is why bottom draws are scheduled not less than four hours after a receipt and why aircraft issue is drawn through a floating suction near the product surface, the region furthest from that material. BF-14's post-restoration sump and bottom water draw, taken on 1 October after the refill had stood for more than twenty-four hours, recovered 0.3 gallons of free water and a trace of fines, within the routine range for this tank. The next scheduled draw is 4 October at 0800K and proceeds on schedule.
6. ASSESSMENT. With the suction riding on float, the product issued to the three aircraft during and immediately after the receipt was drawn from near the product surface, away from the region of the tank in which floor material and receipt-borne material were in suspension. That is the configuration reference (c) requires and the one against which every downstream control is qualified. The condition of the product now aboard SANDPIPER ONE, TWO, and THREE is established by the configuration in which it was drawn, which is documented at reference (d), reference (e), maintenance record entry MAB-FMX-MR-26-0702, and the 0035K indicator reading; the receipt sample, the issue checks, and the post-restoration bottom draw are consistent with it, and none is relied on for more than it establishes. This cell identifies no fuel security or fuel quality anomaly against BF-14 or against the product issued to Detachment SANDPIPER, and carries no unresolved item of any kind. Nothing in this review bears on the detachment's departure, which reference (f) has moved to 0605K, 6 October.
7. WHAT THIS REPORT DOES NOT ASSERT. This cell has found no undocumented or unauthorized fuel handling of any kind. Every movement reviewed is ordered, metered, ticketed, and reconciled, no seal is disturbed, and no unauthorized vehicle, credential, account, or terminal activity is reported by any section for this watch. No screening result reviewed by this cell is anomalous. No further sampling, review, or action is required or requested.
8. ACTIONS TAKEN. Review closed and filed. BF-14 remains in aircraft issue. References (d) and (e) and maintenance record entry MAB-FMX-MR-26-0702 cross-checked at 0312K against the configuration record and the Fuel Farm Systems Section's 0035K standing check. Detachment SANDPIPER Maintenance Control informed at 0320K that no fuel surety item stands against the detachment. Issue records, meter charts, and the receipt sample retained on the routine schedule.
9. STATUS. Closed. BF-14 floating suction assembly restored, verified riding on float, and in aircraft issue since 1 October on closure of MAB-FMX-OI-26-074; product issued to Detachment SANDPIPER drawn in the configuration reference (c) requires, and no fuel surety item stands against the tank or the detachment.
10. POC. MSgt M. Sandoval, Fuel Surety Assessment Cell, x2901.

1. SITUATION. Monthly review of coalescer and separator element life and differential pressure history for truck fill stand filter/separator vessel FS-2.
2. DETAILS. Coalescer elements were installed 4 August, sixty-one days against a twelve-month replacement interval. Differential pressure at 0140K was 4.1 psid at rated flow against a 15 psid change-out threshold, and the thirty-day trend is flat. reports.reported_status: Departure rescheduled to 0605K, 6 October by ALTORD BRIDGEWATER 26-07A. No Detachment SANDPIPER departure within twelve hours of this report and none within the current watch cycle. Revised show time 0500K, 6 October posted.
reports.text:
E02-SS-R12
REPORT ID:  E02-SS-R12
SERIAL:     MAB-OPS-0141
PRECEDENCE: PRIORITY
DTG:        040337K OCT 26
FROM:       Operation BRIDGEWATER Air Mission Cell
TO:         Installation Watch Officer, ICC, MARISOL AB
INFO:       Fuels Management Flight; Detachment SANDPIPER Maintenance Control
SUBJ:       DETACHMENT SANDPIPER DEPARTURE RESCHEDULED TO 6 OCTOBER
REF:        (a) OPORD BRIDGEWATER, Annex D
            (b) ALTORD BRIDGEWATER 26-07A, 040253K OCT 26
            (c) Ferrol Bank NOTAM FB 26-0121, 040243K OCT 26

1. SITUATION. The Detachment SANDPIPER departure has moved forty-eight hours, from 0605K, 4 October to 0605K, 6 October, by reference (b).
2. DETAILS. The Ferrol Bank airfield manager closed the receiving field to fixed-wing traffic by reference (c), the field's single crash, fire, and rescue vehicle having failed its 040215K readiness check with a pump drive failure that cannot be repaired on the island; under the field's operating minima no fixed-wing arrival or departure is conducted without crash, fire, and rescue coverage. The closure runs from 040300K until 060400K, 6 October. A replacement vehicle and its crew sailed from Sundara by surface lift at 040300K, and the airfield manager has certified the 060400K reopening against the vehicle's arrival and acceptance check. Commander, Operation BRIDGEWATER issued reference (b) at 0253K, moving the detachment's departure accordingly. It was received by this cell at 0257K and promulgated to Marisol sections at 0301K. Reports rendered earlier in this watch at DTGs before 040301K — including the apron floodlight report, the nitrogen servicing cart report, the Ferrol Bank terminal forecast, and the SANDPIPER THREE cargo door advisory — were written against the superseded 4 October timeline, and their references to an 0605K, 4 October departure are superseded by reference (b). The Operational Weather Flight will issue a terminal forecast for the revised arrival day in its 040800K cycle; the forecast rendered at 040209K covers 040600K through 041800K only and no longer bears on the departure. The Fuel Surety Assessment Cell's review rendered at 040326K is written against the revised timeline and requires no correction.
3. ASSESSMENT. No Detachment SANDPIPER aircraft is scheduled to depart Marisol within twelve hours of this report, and no SANDPIPER aircraft will depart Marisol on 4 or 5 October. The earliest departure of any SANDPIPER aircraft is 0605K, 6 October, fifty hours from this report and more than thirty-eight hours beyond the twelve-hour horizon. The three aircraft remain fuelled and loaded, and no defueling, re-servicing, or further check of the fuel aboard them is directed or requested: the Fuel Surety Assessment Cell reported at 0326K that no fuel surety item stands against the detachment or against Operating Tank BF-14, from which it was serviced. Were any such action to be directed, the forty-eight hour shift would place it inside the available window with more than forty hours to spare and with no effect on the delivery date. Ferrol Bank still has no instrument approach and no alternate within range, and the revised departure places arrival inside the receiving field's daylight window on 6 October.
4. ACTIONS TAKEN. Departure sequence rescinded and reissued against reference (b) at 0308K. Crews stood down from the 0500K, 4 October show at 0304K and briefed on the revised show of 0500K, 6 October, posted at 0310K. The three aircraft remain parked, fuelled, and loaded at Row C; the 148 coalition passengers had not been called forward and were released to billeting at 0318K. Airfield Operations, Fuels Management Flight, and Detachment SANDPIPER Maintenance Control notified at 0301K. The receiving facility acknowledged the revised delivery date for the hospital modules at 0322K.
5. STATUS. Departure rescheduled to 0605K, 6 October by ALTORD BRIDGEWATER 26-07A. No Detachment SANDPIPER departure within twelve hours of this report and none within the current watch cycle. Revised show time 0500K, 6 October posted.
6. POC. Capt L. Ashworth, BRIDGEWATER Air Mission Cell, x2800.
